LESSON: LABORATORY APPARATUS AND INSTRUMENTS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Scientific Investigation
Topic 1.3: Laboratory apparatus and instruments
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Laboratory apparatus and instruments, part of Scientific Investigation in Grade 7 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why are basic science skills important? 2. How are quantities in science expressed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the meaning and use of basic skills in science,

2. practise use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory, (for heating, measuring mass, temperature, length, volume, weight, magnification, and time) (include parts, functions, and care of a light microscope; and parts of a bunsen burner)

3. collaboratively carry out activities on measurements of basic quantities and express them in the International System of Units (SI) (length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, light intensity),

4. work with peers to carry out activities to determine derived units from basic units (area, volume, speed, density), 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the meaning and use of basic skills in science,
2. practise use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory, (for heating, measuring mass, temperature, length, volume, weight, magnification, and time) (include parts, functions, and care of a light microscope; and parts of a bunsen burner)
3. collaboratively carry out activities on measurements of basic quantities and express them in the International System of Units (SI) (length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, light intensity),
4. work with peers to carry out activities to determine derived units from basic units (area, volume, speed, density), 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Laboratory apparatus and instruments together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: the learner practises the use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory.

● Communication and Collaboration: the learner collaboratively carries out activities on measurements of basic quantities and

expresses them in the International System of Units.

Values:
● Respect: the learner works harmoniously with peers when carrying out activities to determine derived units from basic units

working.

● Responsibility: the learner learns how to care for apparatus and instruments as they practise how to care for and use them in

the laboratory.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Socio-economic issues: the learner links the quantity of goods parked to their prices as they collect packaging with labels of

quantities and discuss the importance of the information on labels

Link to other Learning Areas:

• The learner can link the packaging of goods and labels of quantities from inputs and product labels learnt in Agriculture.

• The learner uses mathematical manipulation skills in recording and carrying out measurements.
